Step-3b authoring keeps the closed case source-backed and the relative-case escape stratum as authored in the lemma; the assembly remains an item for Step 5 review as recorded in the batch notes.

sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 115-page author PDF and verified it against the batch-5 full-text fetch of the same file (3,097,365 bytes, sha256_16 cb69c17956ad7b25). Extracted the full text with mutool and read Lectures 19-21 at PDF pp. 86-101 (lecture-internal pp. 1-16 of the printed notes). Lecture 19 Sec. 6.1: the Morse complex MC_*, the differential, the claim d^2=0 with the compact-one-manifold proof, the definition of MH_*, and the examples (circle, sphere, the comparison MH_*=H_*^{cell}=H_*, and the boundary case). Lecture 19 Sec. 6.2: Morse homology for manifolds with boundary, boundary types a-, b+, the complexes B, d, delta and the long exact sequence of a pair. Lecture 20 Sec. 6.3: the invarian=ce theorem, the continuation moduli C(p-,q+) with the two-end condition, the dimension formula, transversality for generic paths, the chain-map boundary analysis with the two breaking patterns, the energy estimate E(v)=f-(p-)-f+(q+)+ integral of |d_s f_s|, the homotopy-of-homotopies/rogue-trajectory construction and the consequences (1)-(6). Lecture 21 Secs. 7.1-7.4: Poincare duality, Kunneth, the Morse inequalities (corollary, Euler-characteristic lemma, theorem) and the product constructions. Figures and displays were checked against the text; the printed date line is 3 May 2011.

sources.locator: Sec. 2.5 and Sec. 4.4-4.5; printed pp. 62-67 and 183-200 (PDF pp. 72-77 and 193-210)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 291-page author PDF and verified it against the batch-5 full-text fetch of the same file (1,821,860 bytes, sha256_16 c599a63debd5e6e6). Extracted the full text with mutool and read Secs. 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 and 4.4-4.5 at printed pp. 27-33, 46-53, 62-67 and 183-200 (PDF pp. 37-43, 56-63, 72-77, 193-210; printed page = PDF page - 10). Sec. 2.1: handle attachment, the model function with one critical point of index lambda and the trace of surgery. Sec. 2.3: admissible graded vector spaces, Poincare series, the order relation X>Y iff X=Y+(1+t)Q(t) with Q>=0, its equivalence with the alternating-partial-sum inequalities (2.8) and the weak inequalities (2.9), Lemma 2.3.2 (subadditivity of the long exact sequence), Corollary 2.3.3 (topological Morse inequalities P_f>P_M and chi(M)=P_f(-1)), perfectness and the sphere/complex-projective examples. Sec. 2.5: the self-indexing filtration M_k, C_k=H_k(M_k,M_{k-1};Z), the connecting differential, the isomorphism to singular homology, Proposition 2.5.1 (Thom-Smale: d<p| = eps_k sum <p|q><q| with <p|q> the signed intersection/tunnelling count) and Remark 2.5.3 (orientation lines, history, the polyhedral picture of Figure 2.17). Sec. 4.4-4.5: the stratifications of connectors, compactness of the space of broken tunnelings (Proposition 4.4.2), the homeomorphism M(p,q) ~ smooth manifold of dimension lambda(p)-lambda(q)-1 (Proposition 4.4.3), the corners structure (Theorem 4.4.5), the density statements and the dynamic proof of the boundary identity. End of Sec. 4.5, printed p. 200 (PDF p. 210): the theorem of Qin that the pair of the compactified unstable manifold with its boundary is homeomorphic to the pair of closed disks, so that the stratification by unstable manifolds is a CW decomposition and its cellular complex coincides with the Morse-Floer complex.

sources.title: Michael Hutchings, Math 242 Lecture 21: invariance via continuation maps (notes by Jackson Van Dyke, complete PDF)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete four-page lecture note PDF (323,559 bytes, sha256_16 48a109362a91e2e5). Read the whole lecture. Sec. 1.1 defines the compactification of the moduli space of flow lines and the C^infinity-on-compact-sets convergence, with Exercise 1 (subsequential compactness on a compact manifold). Sec. 1.2 states the invariance problem for Morse-Smale pairs, records that (f_t,g_t) cannot be expected to be Morse-Smale for all t, describes Approach 1 (bifurcation analysis) and then Approach 2 (continuation maps, due to Floer): the vector field V(t,x)=beta(t) d/dt + grad f_t on [0,1]xX, the moduli m^V(p_1,p_0) with the dimension formula ind(p_1)-ind(p_0) (with the shifted index at the t=1 end), the definition of psi by counting with signs (or mod 2), Lemma 1 (chain map with the boundary formula (1) and the explicit mod-2 computation), Lemma 2 (independence of the path via a generic homotopy of paths and the chain homotopy K), the identity computation for a constant path (Exercise 2) and the final composition/inverse step. The lecture states the signed count but carries out the detailed computation with Z/2 coefficients.

canonical.support: Constructed from explicit one-dimensional Morse ends and an explicit interpolating field: the ends are the complete Morse-Smale pairs of -x^2/2 and arctan(x)-x^2/2 on the line, and the middle plateau field xdot=-x^2 makes the connecting trajectory escape to +infinity in finite time. sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 115-page author PDF and verified it against the batch-5 full-text fetch of the same file (3,097,365 bytes, sha256_16 cb69c17956ad7b25). Extracted the full text with mutool and read Lectures 19-21 at PDF pp. 86-101 (lecture-internal pp. 1-16 of the printed notes). Lecture 19 Sec. 6.1: the Morse complex MC_*, the differential, the claim d^2=0 with the compact-one-manifold proof, the definition of MH_*, and the examples (circle, sphere, the comparison MH_*=H_*^{cell}=H_*, and the boundary case). Lecture 19 Sec. 6.2: Morse homology for manifolds with boundary, boundary types a-, b+, the complexes B, d, delta and the long exact sequence of a pair. Lecture 20 Sec. 6.3: the invarian=ce theorem, the continuation moduli C(p-,q+) with the two-end condition, the dimension formula, transversality for generic paths, the chain-map boundary analysis with the two breaking patterns, the energy estimate E(v)=f-(p-)-f+(q+)+ integral of |d_s f_s|, the homotopy-of-homotopies/rogue-trajectory construction and the consequences (1)-(6). Lecture 21 Secs. 7.1-7.4: Poincare duality, Kunneth, the Morse inequalities (corollary, Euler-characteristic lemma, theorem) and the product constructions. Figures and displays were checked against the text; the printed date line is 3 May 2011.

sources.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory, 2nd ed. (complete 291-page author PDF)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 291-page author PDF and verified it against the batch-5 full-text fetch of the same file (1,821,860 bytes, sha256_16 c599a63debd5e6e6). Extracted the full text with mutool and read Secs. 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 and 4.4-4.5 at printed pp. 27-33, 46-53, 62-67 and 183-200 (PDF pp. 37-43, 56-63, 72-77, 193-210; printed page = PDF page - 10). Sec. 2.1: handle attachment, the model function with one critical point of index lambda and the trace of surgery. Sec. 2.3: admissible graded vector spaces, Poincare series, the order relation X>Y iff X=Y+(1+t)Q(t) with Q>=0, its equivalence with the alternating-partial-sum inequalities (2.8) and the weak inequalities (2.9), Lemma 2.3.2 (subadditivity of the long exact sequence), Corollary 2.3.3 (topological Morse inequalities P_f>P_M and chi(M)=P_f(-1)), perfectness and the sphere/complex-projective examples. Sec. 2.5: the self-indexing filtration M_k, C_k=H_k(M_k,M_{k-1};Z), the connecting differential, the isomorphism to singular homology, Proposition 2.5.1 (Thom-Smale: d<p| = eps_k sum <p|q><q| with <p|q> the signed intersection/tunnelling count) and Remark 2.5.3 (orientation lines, history, the polyhedral picture of Figure 2.17). Sec. 4.4-4.5: the stratifications of connectors, compactness of the space of broken tunnelings (Proposition 4.4.2), the homeomorphism M(p,q) ~ smooth manifold of dimension lambda(p)-lambda(q)-1 (Proposition 4.4.3), the corners structure (Theorem 4.4.5), the density statements and the dynamic proof of the boundary identity. End of Sec. 4.5, printed p. 200 (PDF p. 210): the theorem of Qin that the pair of the compactified unstable manifold with its boundary is homeomorphic to the pair of closed disks, so that the stratification by unstable manifolds is a CW decomposition and its cellular complex coincides with the Morse-Floer complex.
